issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a subroutine named draw_pixel (Teilaufgabe b), but the provided template and the reference solution both define and call a subroutine named set_pixel. This name mismatch can confuse students about which symbol to implement/call (they may implement draw_pixel while the template expects set_pixel, causing link/assembly errors or runtime failures).
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single, consistent subroutine name across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement to refer to set_pixel instead of draw_pixel, or (B) rename the template and solution subroutine (and all calls) from set_pixel to draw_pixel so the name in the specification matches the code.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a subroutine named draw_pixel (problem_statement.md lines 30-33), while the provided template and reference solution use the name set_pixel for the same routine (template_repository/pixel.asm has a set_pixel stub; solution_repository/pixel.asm implements set_pixel). This naming mismatch refers to the same conceptual entity (the pixel-writing subroutine) but uses two different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students about which symbol to implement or call.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the subroutine name consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) update the problem statement to refer to set_pixel everywhere (replace draw_pixel with set_pixel), or (b) rename the set_pixel label in the template and solution to draw_pixel and update comments accordingly. Apply the chosen name uniformly in instructions, comments, and code so students have a single clear identifier to implement.
